newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ICICI to set up finance company.
newsitem.headline: India's ICICI to set up finance company.

text.p: The Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) said on Thursday its board of directors had approved the setting up of a non-banking finance company (NBFC).
The new firm will be a fully-owned subsidiary of ICICI with a capital base of 500 million rupees, an ICICI statement said.
The subsidiary is expected to create a network of 50 offices in two years with around 6,000 agents in the field, it said.
"One of the issues that ICICI is confronted with is in regard to mobilisation of a large volume of rupee resources," the statement said.
ICICI said this was an area of concern that its institutional shareholders had raised from time to time.

"Going forward, it is felt that a large part of rupee resources will come from retail networks. For this purpose the creation and ownership of a retail distribution network will be the key to establishing competitive advantage," it said.
The setting up of an NBFC would also provide it with a presence in the profitable retail credit market, ICICI said.
"As the subsidiary would be fully owned by ICICI, its accounts are expected to be consolidated in the future," it said.
ICICI is one of India's largest term lenders.
It has leased assets of around 20 billion rupees in industrial equipment leasing, it said.
